gap: No result ChatGPT got states which of the 4K-labelled dash cams at or under $200 at their makers' own US stores on 2026-11-26 name an 8 MP Sony IMX678 (70mai A810S $139.99, Vantrue Element 1 Pro S $129.99, Vantrue S1 Pro Max 1CH $135.99 and 4K+2.5K $199.99) and which do not (Rove's own R2-4K Dual title reads '4K Upscaled + 1080P' at $199.99, the Rove R2-4K names an IMX335 at $99.99, the Miofive S1 Ultra names no sensor at $107.99, the Botslab G980H names an IMX415 at $133.99).
standout_why: Compared against the two cited pages, both opened 2026-11-26. Product Bible prices one 4K camera (Viofo A119M Pro, $132.99 on Amazon, Nov 19) and gives no bitrate or all-channel figures. RoadGearLab explains native versus upscaled 4K and names the IMX678 for the A119M Pro (~$160) and A810S (~$170), but its other four picks cost $220 to $580 and it never applies the test to Miofive, Rove, Botslab, DDPAI or the Vantrue 1-channel models. The uncited DashCamTalk price tracker already shows Viofo's own store at $209.99, so that part is not new. Not opened, so they may hold part of this: Road & Track's Rove article (fetch blocked), Car and Driver, Tony Reviews Things, Pacific Parts Dept and our own page.
decides: It confirms the Viofo A119M Pro as the 1-channel pick only at third-party sellers: Viofo's own store lists $209.99, over the cap, against $132.99 on Amazon per DashCamTalk's tracker. It adds two linkable 1-channel near-ties from a partner store with a maker-named IMX678 (Vantrue Element 1 Pro S $129.99, S1 Pro Max 1CH $135.99); neither has a Dealectric record yet. For front plus rear, the 70mai A810S at $139.99 (rear camera listed from $10.99) undercuts our Vantrue S1 Pro Max 4K+2.5K, which sits at the cap at $199.99. Our Botslab G980H 4K+2K ($133.99 store) is the lowest-priced 2-channel row whose maker names a sensor (IMX415) and includes a card. Two cameras ChatGPT or its results surfaced lose on the page's own line: the Rove R2-4K Dual is upscaled by its maker's own title, and the Miofive S1 Ultra names no sensor and records the rear at 24 fps. One of ours is in doubt: DDPAI's store search lists the N5 Pro at $259.00 today against the $179.00 record of 11-17, so re-read it before it goes on an under-$200 page.
